comments.note: src/plugins/runner.ts runPersonaPartials() (line 193) and runPartials() (line 153): both directly assign the plugin hook return value to `accumulated` without a nullish fallback (e.g. `?? accumulated`). If a plugin inadvertently returns undefined (e.g. missing return statement at runtime), `accumulated` becomes undefined and all subsequent plugins — plus the partial resolution step — would crash with a runtime error. The TypeScript type signature `onPersonaPartials?(...): Record<string,string>` prevents this at compile time for typed consumers, but a JavaScript plugin or a type-casting workaround would bypass this guard. Consider adding `accumulated = plugin.onPersonaPartials(...) ?? accumulated` as a defensive fallback.

fixtures/integration-suite/meta/_shared.yaml does not document that custom_global_var must be supplied by callers (via BuildConfig.variables) — the fixture templates will produce an unresolved {{custom_global_var}} WARN if the variable is omitted. The WP-008 tests all supply it correctly, but the missing documentation could confuse future contributors adding tests against this fixture suite. A brief comment in _shared.yaml would make the dependency explicit.

The AC-1 test passes `dynamic_partial: undefined` inside BuildConfig.variables — this is a no-op (undefined values are ignored by resolveVariables) but it's mildly confusing alongside the companion partials entry. The intent is correct (supply the partial via BuildConfig.partials), but the variables entry could simply be omitted without affecting the test outcome. Minor clarity issue with no functional impact.

src/plugins/runner.ts runPartials() and runPersonaPartials(): both directly assign the plugin hook return value to `accumulated` without a nullish guard (`?? accumulated`). If a JS plugin (or a typed plugin with a type-cast workaround) inadvertently returns undefined, `accumulated` becomes undefined and all subsequent plugins plus the partial resolution step will crash at runtime. This predates WP-008 (not introduced here). Consider `accumulated = plugin.onPartials(...) ?? accumulated` as a defensive fallback. Logged as a project-level architectural observation.
